[[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2007 NCAA Tournament]] }} '''Joakim Simon Noah''' ([[pronunciation]]: ''JO-a-kim'';{{cite web | title=''Star high school athlete becomes his own man''| work=USA TODAY |last=Brady|first=Erik| url=http://www.usatoday.com/news/nation/2004-03-22-noah-basketball_x.htm |date=2004-03-22|accessdate=2007-02-27}} born [[February 25]] [[1985]] in [[New York City]]) is a 6 ft. 11 in. [[United States|American]] [[basketball]] player who played [[College basketball|basketball]] for the [[University of Florida]] in the [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] of the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] from 2004-2007.{{cite web | title=''Joakim Noah Biography'' | work= | url=http://www.joakimnoah.org/joakim-noah-biography.php | accessdate=2007-02-14}} Noah was a member of the Gators' teams that won the [[2006 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2006]] and [[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]]s. ==Early life== Noah is of [[Cameroon|Cameroonian]] descent (his grandfather, Zacharie Noah was a Cameroonian [[Football (soccer)|soccer]] player who had a professional career in France), and of [[French people|French]] and [[Swedish people|Swedish]] descent and nationality, born to [[Yannick Noah]], a former French professional [[tennis]] player and [[1983]] [[French Open (tennis)|French Open]] Champion, and [[Cécilia Rodhe]], [[Miss Sweden]] [[1978]].{{cite web | title=''Joakim Noah Biography'' | work= | url=http://www.joakimnoah.org/joakim-noah-biography.php | accessdate=2007-02-14}}. He competed on basketball teams for several [[high school]]s, first at the [[United Nations International School]] (UNIS) in [[New York City]]. He played streetball tournaments and his nickname was "The Noble One" because someone heard that his dad was a pro tennis player. He later transferred to [[Poly Prep]] in [[Brooklyn]], [[New York]], where he was coached by [[Bill McNally]], and then to [[Lawrenceville School|Lawrenceville]], outside of [[Princeton, New Jersey]]. At UNIS he was coached by Alsonso Shockley and Harry Muniz. He reached the championships as the only sophomore on the team. After that he left to Lawrenceville to further his basketball career. At Lawrenceville, Noah averaged 24.0 points and 12.0 rebounds per game, leading his team to a New Jersey Prep 'A' state title.{{cite web | title=''Joakim Noah Biography'' | work= | url=http://www.joakimnoah.org/joakim-noah-biography.php | accessdate=2007-02-14}} ==College career== During his freshman year at Florida (2004-2005), he played sparingly, clocking in just 10.3 minutes per game, and averaged only 3.9 points and 2.7 rebounds per contest. During his team's two [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]] games, he played a total of 3 minutes.{{cite web | title=''Joakim Noah Biography'' | work= | url=http://www.joakimnoah.org/joakim-noah-biography.php | accessdate=2007-02-14}} During the summer of 2005, he was a key member of the runner-up H3 team at the [[Entertainers Basketball Classic]] at [[Rucker Park]].{{cite web | title=''Joakim Noah Biography'' | work= | url=http://www.joakimnoah.org/joakim-noah-biography.php | accessdate=2007-02-14}} Noah made significant improvement in his sophomore year (2005-2006), leading his team in points (14.2 ppg) and blocks (2.4 bpg), while ranking second in rebounds (7.1 rpg) behind teammate [[Al Horford]] (7.6 rpg). Almost unknown at the beginning of the season, Noah's draft stock improved continually. By the end of the NCAA tournament he was considered by many to be the top college prospect in the country, and had he declared for the [[2006 NBA Draft]] he very likely would have been taken first or second. However, Noah, along with teammates [[Al Horford]] and [[Corey Brewer]] announced at their national championship celebration that they would return for their junior seasons.{{cite web | title=''Joakim Noah Biography'' | work= | url=http://www.joakimnoah.org/joakim-noah-biography.php | accessdate=2007-02-14}} Noah and the Gators would go on to repeat as champions. ==2006 NCAA Tournament== Noah was named the [[NCAA Basketball Tournament Most Outstanding Player|Most Outstanding Player]] (MOP) of the NCAA Tournament's Minneapolis Regional after leading the Gators over top-seeded [[Villanova University|Villanova]] in the final game with 21 points, 15 rebounds, and 5 blocks. On [[April 3]], [[2006]], Noah led the Gators to a 73-57 win over [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]] for the school's first NCAA Basketball Championship, and was named the Most Outstanding Player of the Final Four. In the finale, he posted 16 points, 9 rebounds, and a championship game record 6 blocks. ==International== Though Noah could be eligible for international competitions such as the [[Olympics]] or [[World Basketball Championship]]s by playing with either the [[United States|American]], [[France|French]] or [[Sweden|Swedish]] teams, he seems to be leaning towards playing for [[France]]. "The French National team is definitely something that has been in my dreams for a while."[http://www.draftexpress.com/viewarticle.php?a=2062] Noah is also fluent in French. ==Awards== *2006 [[Associated Press]] (AP) All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] First Team{{cite web|title=''Tide's Steele selected to '06 All-SEC team''|last=Newberry|first=Paul|work=DecaturDaily.com|url=http://www.decaturdaily.com/decaturdaily/sports/060315/steele.shtml|date=2006-03-15|accessdate=2007-03-08}} * Named an Honorable Mention All-American by AP. * A local late night talk show, ''Late Night Gainesville with Zach'', started a campaign in June 2006 to rename a major throughway on the campus of the University of Florida to "Joakim Noah Road." ==Height controversy== Although officially listed on the Gator roster at 6 ft 11 in it is rumored that he is 7 ft 0 in yet refuses to be listed as such as to "not look like a freak"{{Fact|date=May 2007}}. The rumor is substantiated at press conferences where [[Billy Donovan]] has called him 7 ft 0 in on more than one occasion, and [[Woody Paige]] said on [[Around the Horn]] during the 2006 NCAA Tournament that he is 7 ft 0 in. Conflicting this sentiment was an [[ESPN]] report during an [[NBA]] pre-draft workout which reported that he measured at 6 ft 8 in. At the NBA's official 2007 pre-draft camp, Noah's true height measured 6 ft 10.5 in (extended to 7 ft 0 in with the shoes he was wearing that particular day) and he weighed 223 pounds. ==References==
